dedupe_keys.name: iec 61970 301 common information model cim base standard object model of power system resources for utility data exchange

description: IEC 61970-301 sets out the Common Information Model, an abstract model of the major objects in an electric utility enterprise involved in utility operations. It represents power system resources as object classes and attributes with their relationships, so that network applications from different vendors, whole systems, and systems for generation or distribution management can exchange information in a common language independent of their internal representation; SCADA is modelled as far as needed for power system simulation and inter-control-centre communication. The current base publication, IEC 61970-301:2020 from Technical Committee 57, runs to 554 pages, was published on 26 June 2020 and is also sold as a consolidated version with Amendment 1 of 2022. It reflects model version IEC61970CIM17v38 of 21 January 2020 and added feeder modelling, ICCP configuration modelling, corrections from interoperability testing, and annexes on custom extensions, phase-shifting transformer examples and HVDC use cases. The IEC webstore sells it as an electronic document, priced at CHF 475 for a single user, with multi-user copies available, and lists a stability date of 2026. Coverage is global. Caveats: it is a paid standard, not a dataset, and the wider CIM family spans other parts of IEC 61970 and IEC 61968. Simulation uses are a common schema for grid models exchanged between planning, operation and simulation tools and digital twins.
